newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SANITAS JAN-APRIL NET PROFIT FALLS.
newsitem.headline: SANITAS JAN-APRIL NET PROFIT FALLS.

text.p: Lithuania's biggest pharmaceuticals producer Sanitas said on Monday that its net profit in the first four months of 1997 fell despite increases in its sales and production.
The company's director general Albertas Bertulis told Reuters that the company's Jan-April net profit was 3.38 million litas compared to 4.5 million litas in the same period in last year.
Production output during the first four months of the year was 16.1 million litas compared to 15 million litas in the same period the previous year, he said.
He added that the company's sales rose to 14.7 million litas in the first four months of the year from 14.2 million litas in the same period last year.
The company reported earlier that its net profit in the first quarter of 1997 was 2.2 million litas at its output was 11.8 million litas.
"Our net profit in April increased after our partners in Russia were issued licenses to sell our products in Russia," Bertulis said.
Bertulis said that the company planned to retain the same sales level throughout the year but the government's cut to profit tax privileges will make it difficult to maintain the smae profit level.
The company's net profit in 1996 was 10.74 million litas.
The company exports 90 percent of its products, 75 percent to Russia.
Sanitas is listed on the A group of the Vilnius bourse.
